$description: Shared primitive tokens. Neither internal-operator nor customer token sets duplicate a value defined here — they only reference or override it. Derived per Doc 60 §4 'tokens/' instruction. Color RAMPS are primitives; SEMANTIC color roles (bg, text, border, accent) are assigned per theme in the two theme files, because a role's mapping to a ramp step differs between the dense internal context and the airier customer context (Doc 56 §5.1).

color.$comment: Two ramps: a neutral (slate, slightly cool-toned so it never reads as 'default grey') and a brand teal used for the accent role in both themes. Contrast pairs below are pre-verified against WCAG 2.1 AA (4.5:1 body text, 3:1 large text/UI) — see handoff/accessibility-contrast-matrix.md for the verification table.

amber.$comment: Semantic-warning ramp, distinct from the teal accent per Doc 56's 'semantic color is separate from the accent hue' discipline.

blue.$comment: Used only for 'informational' semantic states (e.g. shadow-mode badges) — never repurposed as the accent.

display.$comment: Headings, screen titles, the Escalation Review header sentence.

mono.$comment: Run IDs, blueprint versions, PO/invoice line-item figures, anything tabular-numeric.

scale.$comment: A type scale shared by both themes; the CUSTOMER theme uses one step larger at each rank for body/label sizes per its 'more whitespace, plainer' brief (see customer.tokens.json).

spacing.$comment: 4px base unit. Named, not just numbered, so a component spec can say 'gap: spacing.gap-tight' and a reviewer can tell intent from the token name.

lg.$comment: Modals, the Escalation Review screen's evidence panel container.

full.$comment: Pills — used ONLY for status pills, never for buttons (buttons use md, per handoff/design-log.md decision #2).

shadow.$comment: Elevation is spent sparingly per artifact-design guidance — only the modal/inline-editor layer and the Teams-card-equivalent 'floating' surfaces get a shadow. Flat panels (the evidence panel itself) use a border, not a shadow, to read as part of the page rather than floating above it.

motion.$comment: Durations only — the Escalation Review screen and Fleet Overview grid both favor near-instant feedback (Doc 56 §2.1 'seconds, not minutes'); nothing in this system uses a duration above 'moderate,' and decorative motion is out of scope entirely per the design brief's fidelity-to-Doc-56 constraint.

breakpoint.$comment: The Console is a behind-login SPA (Doc 56 §1.1) used primarily on desktop/laptop by reviewers and operators at a desk. Two breakpoints, not five — this is a working tool, not a marketing site.

compact.$comment: Down to a tablet in portrait — supports a reviewer clearing the Approval Queue from a tablet between meetings.

wide.$comment: The default authoring/reviewing width; the Fleet Overview matrix and the Escalation Review's side-by-side evidence panel both assume this width or greater as their primary target.
